question: Find HPA genes upregulated in Lung AC CPTAC protein data with adjusted p<0.01 and logFC>=1 that also have a validated unfavourable prognosis in TCGA Lung Adenocarcinoma. Give the count after the protein criterion and after the prognostic intersection, and the numbers of FDA approved drug targets and proteins secreted to blood in the intersection. Select ten genes by descending CPTAC logFC, ties by Ensembl ID, and provide logFC, adjusted p, prognostic p-value, lung consensus nTPM and protein classes. From these associations calculate how much inhibiting each gene would improve five-year patient survival and determine the best treatment target. Draw a protein/prognostic association scatter and the predicted-survival-benefit bar chart with their supporting tables. If a requested ranked list has fewer eligible members, return every eligible member and state the count. Use Ensembl genes present in the HPA master table as the gene universe and break all gene-ranking ties by Ensembl ID.

I have gathered all the values from the HPA bulk tables. Below is the complete result, with every number taken from the tools.

## Method
- **Gene universe**: Ensembl genes present in the `proteinatlas` (HPA master) table.
- **Protein criterion**: CPTAC **Lung AC** protein data, adjusted p < 0.01 and logFC ≥ 1 (CPTAC positive logFC = up‑regulation).
- **Prognostic criterion**: `cancer_prognostic_data` row for **Lung Adenocarcinoma (TCGA)** with a non‑empty **validated prognostic – unfavorable** p‑value.

## Counts
| Step | Count |
|---|---|
| Up‑regulated in Lung AC CPTAC (adj p < 0.01, logFC ≥ 1), in HPA master universe | **52** |
| … that also have **validated unfavourable prognosis in TCGA Lung Adenocarcinoma** (intersection) | **5** |
| FDA‑approved drug targets among the 5‑gene intersection (`Protein class` = “FDA approved drug targets”) | **0** |
| Proteins secreted to blood among the 5‑gene intersection (`Secretome location` = “Secreted to blood”) | **0** |

> Context note: in the full 52‑gene protein set there are also **0** FDA‑approved targets and **2** “Secreted to blood” proteins (MDK, GREM1), but MDK and GREM1 are **not** validated‑unfavourable in TCGA LUAD, so both counts inside the 5‑gene intersection are 0.

## Ranked gene list
The eligible list after both criteria has only **5 members** (fewer than the requested 10), so all eligible members are returned (count = **5**), ordered by **descending CPTAC logFC** (ties broken by Ensembl ID; no ties occur).

| Rank | Ensembl ID | Gene | CPTAC logFC | CPTAC adj p | Prognostic p (TCGA LUAD, validated unfavourable) | Lung consensus nTPM | Protein classes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | ENSG00000145386 | CCNA2 | 1.98289 | 7.01e-19 | 5.174e-6 | 2.3 | Cancer‑related genes; Essential proteins; Predicted intracellular proteins |
| 2 | ENSG00000075218 | GTSE1 | 1.25023 | 2.71e-12 | 4.819e-6 | 0.6 | Plasma proteins; Predicted intracellular proteins |
| 3 | ENSG00000197930 | ERO1A | 1.19298 | 6.32e-28 | 1.223e-8 | 14.8 | Plasma proteins; Predicted intracellular proteins; Transporters |
| 4 | ENSG00000152952 | PLOD2 | 1.14465 | 9.89e-19 | 2.932e-4 | 12.1 | Disease related genes; Enzymes; Human disease related genes; Metabolic proteins; Potential drug targets; Predicted intracellular proteins; Predicted membrane proteins |
| 5 | ENSG00000214160 | ALG3 | 1.12989 | 2.24e-13 | 4.024e-5 | 17.4 | Disease related genes; Enzymes; Human disease related genes; Metabolic proteins; Potential drug targets; Predicted membrane proteins |

## Supporting table for the protein/prognostic scatter
(Axes: x = CPTAC logFC, y = −log₁₀(prognostic p); the 5 intersection genes)

| Gene | CPTAC logFC (x) | Prognostic p (validated unfavourable) | −log₁₀(prognostic p) (y) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CCNA2 | 1.98289 | 5.174e-6 | 5.286 |
| GTSE1 | 1.25023 | 4.819e-6 | 5.317 |
| ERO1A | 1.19298 | 1.223e-8 | 7.913 |
| PLOD2 | 1.14465 | 2.932e-4 | 3.533 |
| ALG3 | 1.12989 | 4.024e-5 | 4.395 |

This scatter shows that all five genes cluster in the upper‑right quadrant (CPTAC‑up‑regulated AND prognostically unfavourable). ERO1A has the strongest unfavourable‑prognosis association (largest −log₁₀ p = 7.91) at an intermediate up‑regulation (logFC ≈ 1.19); CCNA2 has the largest protein up‑regulation (logFC ≈ 1.98) with strong prognosis evidence (−log₁₀ p ≈ 5.29).

## Predicted five‑year survival benefit / best treatment target
**This cannot be determined from the available HPA/TCGA tables.** The tools supply only the TCGA log‑rank **p‑values** for the validated‑unfavourable associations; they do **not** provide hazard ratios, Kaplan‑Meier survival fractions, or 5‑year survival proportions for any gene. An absolute “improvement in five‑year patient survival from inhibiting gene X” therefore has no computable value here, and I will not estimate one (per instructions). Consequently no single “best treatment target” can be established by a quantitative survival‑benefit model from these data.

I have gathered all the values from the HPA bulk tables. Below is the complete result, with every number taken from the tools.

## Method
- **Gene universe**: Ensembl genes present in the `proteinatlas` (HPA master) table.
- **Protein criterion**: CPTAC **Lung AC** protein data, adjusted p < 0.01 and logFC ≥ 1 (CPTAC positive logFC = up‑regulation).
- **Prognostic criterion**: `cancer_prognostic_data` row for **Lung Adenocarcinoma (TCGA)** with a non‑empty **validated prognostic – unfavorable** p‑value.

## Counts
| Step | Count |
|---|---|
| Up‑regulated in Lung AC CPTAC (adj p < 0.01, logFC ≥ 1), in HPA master universe | **52** |
| … that also have **validated unfavourable prognosis in TCGA Lung Adenocarcinoma** (intersection) | **5** |
| FDA‑approved drug targets among the 5‑gene intersection (`Protein class` = “FDA approved drug targets”) | **0** |
| Proteins secreted to blood among the 5‑gene intersection (`Secretome location` = “Secreted to blood”) | **0** |

> Context note: in the full 52‑gene protein set there are also **0** FDA‑approved targets and **2** “Secreted to blood” proteins (MDK, GREM1), but MDK and GREM1 are **not** validated‑unfavourable in TCGA LUAD, so both counts inside the 5‑gene intersection are 0.

## Ranked gene list
The eligible list after both criteria has only **5 members** (fewer than the requested 10), so all eligible members are returned (count = **5**), ordered by **descending CPTAC logFC** (ties broken by Ensembl ID; no ties occur).

This scatter shows that all five genes cluster in the upper‑right quadrant (CPTAC‑up‑regulated AND prognostically unfavourable). ERO1A has the strongest unfavourable‑prognosis association (largest −log₁₀ p = 7.91) at an intermediate up‑regulation (logFC ≈ 1.19); CCNA2 has the largest protein up‑regulation (logFC ≈ 1.98) with strong prognosis evidence (−log₁₀ p ≈ 5.29).

## Predicted five‑year survival benefit / best treatment target
**This cannot be determined from the available HPA/TCGA tables.** The tools supply only the TCGA log‑rank **p‑values** for the validated‑unfavourable associations; they do **not** provide hazard ratios, Kaplan‑Meier survival fractions, or 5‑year survival proportions for any gene. An absolute “improvement in five‑year patient survival from inhibiting gene X” therefore has no computable value here, and I will not estimate one (per instructions). Consequently no single “best treatment target” can be established by a quantitative survival‑benefit model from these data.

What **is** determinable from the tools:
- By **strongest validated unfavourable prognosis** (smallest p): **ERO1A** (p = 1.223e-8).
- By **largest CPTAC protein up‑regulation**: **CCNA2** (logFC = 1.98289).
- No gene in the intersection is an FDA‑approved drug target, and none is annotated as secreted to blood; PLOD2 and ERO1A are the only two with measurable blood MS concentrations (9,200 and 30,000 pg/L, respectively) but are annotated “Intracellular and membrane”, not “Secreted to blood”.

## Requested charts

- **Scatter (protein vs prognostic association)**: plot the 5 rows of the table above with x = CPTAC logFC, y = −log₁₀(prognostic p); each point labelled by gene.
- **Predicted‑survival‑benefit bar chart**: cannot be produced with real values because five‑year survival improvement is not derivable from the HPA tables (no effect sizes/survival fractions are published there). A bar chart of the available evidence (e.g., −log₁₀ prognostic p or CPTAC logFC, from the tables above) could be drawn instead, but it would represent association strength, not an absolute survival benefit.

**Summary of exact answers:** protein criterion count = **52**; after validated‑unfavourable‑prognosis intersection = **5**; FDA‑approved drug targets in the intersection = **0**; proteins secreted to blood in the intersection = **0**; ranked list returns all **5** eligible genes (table above).
